# Curriculum coverage inventory - Danish category B

> Audit boundary: this is a machine-assisted objective-level candidate inventory for the current app snapshot. Statuses describe metadata and lexical signals for manual review. None has been verified by a qualified driving instructor, and no status shows full teaching, practical competence, legal approval, or complete curriculum coverage.

## Source verification

- Authority page: https://www.fstyr.dk/publikationer/undervisningsplan-for-kategori-b
- Official PDF: https://cdn.fstyr.dk/faerdselsstyrelsen/Media/639159124710541258/undervisningsplan-kategori-b-almindelig-bil-version-11-maj-2026_pdf290526.pdf
- Authority page states effective from **2026-07-01**.
- Local and live official PDF were byte-identical on 2026-10-16: 7131928 bytes; SHA-256 `8f4160ce8e8f55625af8cbe178ab3d1ba67927809d9662834f150007a501f26c`.
- Extraction covers 206 detailed sections and 1902 numbered objectives from 1.1.1 through 10.3.2.

## Status model

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `direct` | **Exact-reference candidate:** a lesson or Garage item explicitly cites the exact numbered objective. The content itself has not been instructor-verified against the objective. |
| `partial` | **Automated lexical candidate:** content in the same detailed section shares terms with the objective but lacks an exact objective reference. |
| `needs-review` | **Broad-section candidate:** only section-level metadata exists; objective-level equivalence requires manual subject-matter review. |
| `missing` | **No mapped candidate:** current metadata has no item mapped to the detailed official section; this does not prove that no related prose exists elsewhere. |

## New authoring exemplar: hidden cyclist at a right turn

Status: **runtime-implemented-pending-qualified-review**. The runtime lesson exists in `dist/turn-learning.js` and `dist/turn-lesson.js`, but its curriculum/legal interpretation still awaits qualified review.

Official anchors: `7.13.3.5`, `7.13.3.11`, `7.13.3.12`, `7.13.3.19`, `7.13.3.21`, `7.13.4.10`, `7.13.4.11`.

Anchor roles: hidden rear-right cyclist hazard: `7.13.3.5`; right-turn conditions and cyclist placement: `7.13.3.11`; mirror and blind-angle checks before positioning: `7.13.3.12`; repeat rearward and blind-angle checks before turning: `7.13.3.19`, `7.13.3.21`; yield to straight-ahead cyclists: `7.13.4.10`, `7.13.4.11`.

Current runtime label: `Undervisningsplan for kategori B, version 1.1 (maj 2026), afsnit 7.13.3, pkt. 5, 11-12, 19 og 21, samt 7.13.4, pkt. 10-11.`.

Previous label (retired): `Plan B 7.13.3, pkt. 11–14 og 19–21`

Source-label finding: The retired label omitted 7.13.4 points 10-11, which support yielding to straight-ahead cyclists, and included 7.13.3 points 13-14 and 20, which are not directly demonstrated by the main hidden-cyclist decision. The current label is corrected; runtime/browser synchronization remains an evidence item.

Transfer-case boundary: The right-of-way instruction is directly supported by current Færdselsloven § 26, stk. 6, 2. og 5. pkt.: the same-direction cyclist rule expressly also applies when driving across or leaving the roadway outside a junction. As curriculum taxonomy, the driveway remains a transfer case beyond the intersection wording of Plan B 7.13.

### Primary legal source for the driveway transfer

- Current act: [Bekendtgørelse af færdselsloven, LBK nr. 118 af 12. januar 2026](https://www.retsinformation.dk/eli/lta/2026/118) (Gældende; checked 2026-10-16).
- Exact anchor: `Færdselsloven, LBK nr. 118 af 12. januar 2026, § 26, stk. 6, 2. og 5. pkt. (jf. § 17, stk. 1, og § 16, stk. 2)`
- Section 26(6), relevant text: “Ved svingning til højre må den kørende ikke være til ulempe for cyklister og knallertkørere, der kører lige ud. Tilsvarende regler gælder ved kørsel over eller bort fra kørebanen uden for vejkryds.”
- Companion general rule: Section 17(1) extends section 16(1)-(3) outside junctions; section 16(2) requires the manoeuvre to be possible without danger or unnecessary inconvenience to others travelling in the same direction.
- Application: For a right turn from the roadway into a property driveway outside a junction, across a parallel continuous cycle track, section 26(6) applies expressly through its final sentence. The driver must not inconvenience a same-direction cyclist continuing straight.
- Boundary: This conclusion assumes “indkørsel” means a property driveway reached by leaving the roadway. If it is actually a side road forming a junction, the ordinary right-turn sentence in section 26(6) still applies. Section 26(3) concerns traffic coming out from property or similar areas and is not the anchor for entering the property.

The runtime-file mapping above was reviewed manually and is not included in the automated status counts.

**Lead:** A cyclist who disappears behind a van or into the car’s blind angle has not disappeared from the conflict path.

- **Find the cyclist again:** Check mirrors early, then repeat the direct blind-angle check immediately before crossing the cycle path. Do not infer a free path from a missing reflection.
- **The obstacle changes sight, not priority:** A parked van can hide movement toward the junction. Wait until the cyclist is seen again or the entire expected path can be established as clear.
- **Hold back before the turn:** If the cyclist is beside the car or can reach the conflict point, remain behind and turn only when the cyclist has continued straight and the path is free.

**Case:** You are waiting to turn right. A cyclist you saw behind the car becomes hidden first by a parked van and then at the car’s right rear corner. **Action:** Stay stopped, repeat mirror and direct blind-angle checks, and turn only after locating the cyclist and confirming the cycle path is free. **Why:** The cyclist may continue toward the same conflict point and must not be forced to slow or stop because of the turn.

**Recall:** What does it mean when a cyclist disappears from the mirror before a right turn? It is a reason to search again, not evidence that the cyclist is gone.

Existing related app evidence: section sving-cykel; question q-014; lesson case in sving-cykel; runtime lesson “Et blink. To baner.”.

## Traceability boundary

Every official objective row includes explicit source, explanation, scenario, facit, and validation fields. `candidate` means a linked app artifact exists; it does not claim that the artifact teaches or assesses the objective adequately. `missing` and `null` identify an absent artifact. Qualified review and human evidence remain pending.

Flagship lesson map: `authoring/turn-lesson-map.json` with 7 explicitly linked objectives and bounded browser evidence for risk, repair, transfer, contrast, recall, reload, and final evidence; all seven remain pending qualified review and human efficacy.

## Extraction and interpretation limits

- The inventory treats each numbered bullet inside detailed sections 1.1.1-10.3.2 as an objective. It does not split unnumbered main goals, explanatory prose, or cross-references into extra rows.
- Five detailed sections have no numbered objective in the PDF because the plan defers those subjects to later manoeuvres: 7.2.1, 7.2.2, 7.4.1, 7.10.1, and 7.11.1.
- Official text is extracted from the PDF with line-wrap dehyphenation. The JSON retains page and section locators so any questionable wording can be checked against the source.
- Every status is a candidate classification. `direct` is based only on an exact metadata reference; `partial` is automated lexical matching; `needs-review` is broad section metadata; `missing` is absence from the mapped metadata set.
- No objective row has received qualified driving-instructor verification. Statuses are review queues, not claims of factual correctness, teaching completeness, or curriculum approval.
- Practical objectives cannot be completed or certified by this app. The inventory records only digital content touchpoints.

| 1.2.3.4 | Blokeringsfri bremser (ABS) er indrettet således, at de hindrer hjulene i at blokere under bremsning og muliggør dermed i en vis udstrækning styring og bremsning samtidig. Ved hjulene på en bil med ABS-bremser sidder der følere, der registrerer hjulets omdrejninger og sender impulser til en elektronisk styreboks. Hvis et eller flere hjul under opbremsning har tendens til at blokere, vil den elektroniske styreboks regulere trykket til bremserne således, at blokering af hjulet(ene) undgås. Denne regulering giver vibrationer i bremsepedalen. | 7.11.3.37 | »Hovedsignaler« (X 11): a) rødt lys betyder stop, og at man skal stoppe ved stoplinje eller i sikker afstand fra krydset, hvis der ikke er stoplinje. Rødt og gult lys samtidig betyder ligeledes stop, men angiver desuden, at signalet snart skifter til grønt, b) grønt lys betyder kør, hvis vejen er fri. Fremkørsel for grønt lys er dog ikke tilladt, hvis færdslen forhindrer, at man kan komme helt over krydset og dermed spærrer for den tværgående færdsel, når signalet skifter, c) gult lys betyder stop og angiver desuden, at signalet snart skifter til rødt. ### 7.18.5 Lovbestemmelser i øvrigt

| 7.21.3.7 | »Bus- og letbanesignal samt signal for nulemissionsbil« (X 19). Signalet har hvidt lys i alle tre lysåbninger. Lys i øverste, øverste og midterste, midterste og nederste åbning har samme betydning som henholdsvis rødt, rødt og gult, gult og grønt lys. Den hvide bjælke i nederste åbning kan vise skråt opad til højre eller skråt opad til venstre. Lys i nederste åbning har da samme betydning som grønt pilsignal henholdsvis til højre eller til venstre, jf. »Pilsignal« (X 12). Bus- og letbanesignal gælder for busser i rutekørsel og for letbanekøretøjer samt for nulemissionsbiler. Øverste lysåbning kan udelades, når signalerne opsættes sammen med »Hovedsignal« (X 11). Signalet kan være suppleret med cifre, der angiver tid til skift til grønt for rutebusser og for letbanekøretøjer samt for nulemissionsbiler. | 8.1.2.1 | Forskellige typer narkotiske stoffer har følgende indvirkning på færdselssikkerheden: a) stimulerende stoffer øger aktivitetsniveauet. Man mærker ikke træthed og har en øget risikoadfærd, så man fx tager chancer og laver fejlvurderinger med en øget risiko for trafikuheld til følge. De hyppigst forekommende stimulerende stoffer er: i) amfetamin (speed), ii) kokain, iii) ecstasy og en række syntetisk fremstillede rusmidler, såkaldte designerdrugs. Nogle af disse kan også medføre hallucinationer, b) sløvende stoffer medfører nedsat opmærksomhed, koordinationsevne og reaktionshastighed, hvilket medfører øget risiko for trafikuheld. De hyppigst forekommende sløvende stoffer er: i) cannabis (hash, marihuana, pot), ii) heroin, morfin, metadon (opioider), iii) anden stærk smertestillende medicin, iv) sove- og nervemedicin (benzodiazepiner som fx stesolid), v) ghb (fantasy), vi) lattergas, c) stoffer, der giver hallucinationer, medfører en forvrænget virkelighedsopfattelse, hvilket øger risikoen for trafikuheld.
